drivingQuestion: Why do the Rabbis not designate another wife if they designate another priest?
outcomeNote: the Rabbis' distinction between common impurity and uncommon death answers the difficulty

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף אִשָּׁה אַחֶרֶת מַתְקִינִין לוֹ. וְרַבָּנַן נָמֵי, הָא חָיְישִׁי לְשֶׁמָּא? אָמְרִי לָךְ רַבָּנַן: טוּמְאָה שְׁכִיחָא, מִיתָה לָא שְׁכִיחָא.
segments.en: § It was taught in the mishna that «Rabbi Yehuda says:» The Sages would «even designate another wife for» the High Priest lest his wife die. The Rabbis say: There is no concern lest his wife die, and therefore the Sages did not designate another wife for him. The Gemara asks with regard to «the Rabbis: Aren’t they concerned lest» he become impure, which is why the Sages designate a replacement High Priest? Why then, are they not concerned lest his wife die? The Gemara answers that «the Rabbis» could have «said to you: Impurity is common,» as it is not unusual for the High Priest to become impure either due to secretions from his body or from an external source. «Death is not common,» and therefore there is no concern lest his wife die.
